cards.title: Introduction to Bean Validation
cards.content:
Validation is a critical aspect of any application to ensure data integrity. In Spring Boot, validation is built on top of the Jakarta Bean Validation specification (formerly JSR 380), with Hibernate Validator serving as the default implementation.

To get started, you must include the starter dependency in your pom.xml:

<dependency>
  <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
  <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-validation</artifactId>
</dependency>

cards.title: Common Validation Annotations
cards.content:
Bean Validation provides several built-in annotations that you can apply directly to your fields:

  • @NotNull: Checks that the annotated value is not null.
  • @NotEmpty: Checks that the annotated property is not null and not empty (works for Strings, Collections).
  • @NotBlank: Checks that the annotated string is not null and its trimmed length is greater than zero.
  • @Size(min=, max=): Validates that the size of a string, collection, or map is within the boundaries.
  • @Min / @Max: Validates numeric values boundaries.
  • @Email: Asserts that the string is a well-formed email address.

cards.title: Triggering Validation in Controllers
cards.content:
To instruct Spring Boot to validate incoming payloads, you must annotate incoming RequestBody parameter with the @Valid annotation.

@PostMapping("/users")
public ResponseEntity<String> createUser(@Valid @RequestBody UserDto userDto) {
    return ResponseEntity.ok("User is valid!");
}

If validation fails, Spring Boot automatically throws a MethodArgumentNotValidException and returns a 400 Bad Request status.

cards.title: Creating Custom Validators
cards.content:
When built-in annotations are not enough, you can create a custom constraint. This requires two main components:

  1. An annotation interface declared with @Constraint(validatedBy = CustomValidator.class).
  2. A validator class implementing ConstraintValidator<Annotation, FieldType>.
@Target({ElementType.FIELD})
@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)
@Constraint(validatedBy = IpAddressValidator.class)
public @interface IpAddress {
    String message() default "Invalid IP Address";
    Class<?>[] groups() default {};
    Class<?>[] payload() default {};
}

cards.title: Handling Validation Exceptions
cards.content:
By default, Spring Boot returns a standard error layout when validation fails. To customize the payload structure, you can use @RestControllerAdvice alongside an @ExceptionHandler for MethodArgumentNotValidException.

@RestControllerAdvice
public class GlobalExceptionHandler {
    @ExceptionHandler(MethodArgumentNotValidException.class)
    public ResponseEntity<Map<String, String>> handleValidationExceptions(MethodArgumentNotValidException ex) {
        Map<String, String> errors = new HashMap<>();
        ex.getBindingResult().getFieldErrors().forEach(error -> 
            errors.put(error.getField(), error.getDefaultMessage()));
        return ResponseEntity.badRequest().body(errors);
    }
}

cards.title: Order of execution in Spring Boot Validation

content.instruction: Order the lifecycle phases of a request with invalid data entering your application:

items.text: The incoming HTTP Request reaches the DispatcherServlet
Spring binds the request payload data to the Java object
The @Valid processor invokes validation annotations checking field rules
MethodArgumentNotValidException is raised due to validation failures
The @RestControllerAdvice captures the exception and serializes a structured JSON error response

cards.title: Validation Groups
cards.content:
Sometimes, validation requirements differ depending on the application state. For example, a User ID must be null during user creation, but cannot be null during updates.

Using Validation Groups, you can assign constraints to specific interfaces:

public interface OnCreate {}
public interface OnUpdate {}

public class UserDto {
    @Null(groups = OnCreate.class)
    @NotNull(groups = OnUpdate.class)
    private Long id;
}

In the Controller, use @Validated(OnCreate.class) instead of @Valid to activate only creation rules.
